claims.statement: From 9 July 2027, Member State authorities must accept freight information shared electronically through certified eFTI platforms.
Official architecture expects secure certified platforms integrated with existing business systems, with inspection access through unique machine-readable links such as QR codes.
Demand hypothesis: smaller TMS vendors will buy a shared adapter because becoming and maintaining a certified platform is outside their core product scope.

contrary_evidence: Businesses are not necessarily compelled to use electronic freight information even when authorities must accept it.
Certified platforms may provide their own low-cost connectors directly to TMS vendors.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: integrate with 10-20 regional TMS vendors instead of selling directly to thousands of carriers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 60 TMS vendors averaging 90000 PLN annual recurring revenue plus usage could exceed 7m PLN ARR; multi-platform compatibility and embedded volume could support founder equity above 5m PLN in 5-7 years
economics.founder_time: 18-25 hours weekly through one TMS and one certified-platform pilot
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 75-88% net of certified-platform wholesale fees
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 14-20 months with ten TMS customers and 100000 monthly consignments
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 3000-12000 PLN monthly per TMS vendor plus 0.50-3 PLN per consignment
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every regulated consignment and continuing schema, authority and platform updates

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable mappings across Polish TMS schemas, freight data sets and certified-platform endpoints improve with each integration
fingerprint.customer: Polish TMS vendors and road-freight networks serving SMEs with cross-border or regulated freight
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: One integration distributes through each TMS vendor's installed carrier base
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Multi-platform schema adapter, validation engine and audit-log API sold wholesale to TMS vendors
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: TMS vendor or carrier network pays connector subscription and per compliant consignment
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A transport record must be presented electronically through a certified platform when authorities begin mandatory acceptance

founder_fit: API mapping, validation and audit logs fit technical strengths
B2B infrastructure can be sold through a small number of software channels
A connector MVP stays within available capital if certification is delegated
risks: Final specifications or certification economics may change.
Dependence on a small number of certified platform partners
Long enterprise and public-transport adoption cycles

structure.control_point: The validated consignment payload and authority access link generated before dispatch
structure.critical_dependency: Commercial access to certified eFTI platforms and stable final technical specifications

thesis: Rather than funding a full certified platform, a narrow adapter could let Polish transport-management vendors map, validate and transmit customer freight records through one or more certified eFTI platforms, returning the authority access link and audit trail. The adapter depends on certified partners and makes no certification claim. Demand and economics are hypotheses.
title: eFTI Certified-Platform Adapter for Polish TMS Vendors
uncertainties: Fragmentation of Polish TMS schemas and reachable consignment volume
